alternatives_considered.approach: Move the expense-row relative labels into client islands that read the viewer's clock (the review's second option).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A larger diff touching server/client boundaries for every row to fix what the absolute-date suffix already makes never-wrong; the rows stay server-rendered and deterministic.

alternatives_considered.approach: Truncate the activity action sentence with ellipsis and a title attribute like expense ListRows do.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Feed sentences are audit text whose actor and action must stay readable; wrapping keeps the full sentence while still eliminating the horizontal scroll, whereas ellipsis would hide exactly the description QA needs to see.

alternatives_considered.approach: Plan a code fix for the refused-save include-switch reset anyway (re-applying flags from the submitted form after a refusal).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no writer of all-included state in the current code to counteract: re-applying from DOM or action state would be a no-op over state that already holds the flags, so a blind fix changes behaviour without a mechanism and risks the editor for nothing.

work_order.approach: Fix the four claims that reproduce in current code with the smallest change that removes each root cause, and drop the one claim that has no mechanism. Make humanDateLabel append the absolute day-month to the relative word so server rows are never wrong (one function, both call sites fixed), and compute the editor's today from the viewer's local calendar date instead of toISOString. Give the IncludeSwitch label a 44px hit area with no visual change. Gate both revalidateBalances calls in lib/settle/actions.ts on outcome.groupId and make the parameter required so a future success path cannot silently skip invalidation. Wrap activity-feed text lines with break-words/min-w-0 instead of truncating them. Drop the refused-save include-reset claim with written reasoning and a QA re-verification step, since every editor field lives in one useState array whose values QA confirms persist.
assumptions: QA can run the browser checks in a non-UTC timezone (or emulate one) to observe the viewer-clock behavior; the unit tests pin the label format independent of zone.

No existing e2e or snapshot asserts the exact strings 'Today', 'Yesterday' or 'Tomorrow' outside lib/money/human-date.test.ts (grep shows only that file references the function besides its two render call sites).
work_order.confidence_rationale: Four of five findings confirmed line-by-line in current main with minimal, well-understood fixes; the fifth is dropped with an explicit impossibility argument rather than a guess. The main uncertainty is the editor-local-date change interacting with existing date-hint expectations, covered by unit tests plus a browser AC.
work_order.debate_summary: The choice that mattered was the relative-date fix shape: a client island per row would give viewer-exact relative words but costs server/client complexity on every row, while appending the absolute date makes the row never wrong for a few characters. The review offered both and the lighter one wins here. Likewise wrapping versus ellipsis in the feed: the sentence is evidence, so it wraps.

Non-relative and unreadable inputs return exactly as today. Update the doc comment to state the row is never wrong, only less chatty, for viewers away from UTC.

Refusals, which return no groupId, then revalidate nothing, restoring the previous refusal behavior; both success paths still revalidate '/', '/activity' and the group pages.

No truncation: feed sentences stay fully readable.

out_of_scope: Refused-save include-switch reset (QA finding 4): dropped, not planned. All editor fields including the included flags live in one useState array with no resync effect, no key and no redirect on refusal, so no code path replaces the flags; a remount would reset the text values too, which QA confirms persist. Expense/group action revalidation (lib/expenses/actions.ts revalidateGroup, lib/groups/actions.ts): same optional-guard shape as the settle defect, but not named by this issue; changing them here widens scope. Own ticket if wanted.

issue_snapshot.title: Follow-ups from #36: 3 from the review, 2 from QA
issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #43 (for #36) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot.

## From the review

Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong.

### Expense-row relative dates ('Today'/'Yesterday'/'Tomorrow') are computed from the server's UTC clock, so they can be off by one for viewers away from UTC.

> Expense-row relative dates ('Today'/'Yesterday'/'Tomorrow') are computed from the server's UTC clock, so they can be off by one for viewers away from UTC.
> 
> `app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:236`
> 
> Evidence: app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:236 `const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (UTC) feeds humanDateLabel at :555. toISOString is UTC: a viewer at UTC-8 reading the group page at 6pm local sees server-tomorrow, so today's expenses read 'Yesterday'. The editor avoids this by reading the clock client-side post-mount; the server-rendered rows cannot, and the relative word replaces (not accompanies) the absolute date.
> 
> Fix: Render the absolute day-month next to the relative word on server rows (so the row is never wrong, only less chatty), or move the relative label into a tiny client island that reads the viewer's day.

### The restyled per-member include switch shrank its touch target below the ui.md 44px minimum: the label carries no min-height and the visible track is h-6 (24px tall), where the control it replaces sat in a min-h-11 (44px) label.

> The restyled per-member include switch shrank its touch target below the ui.md 44px minimum: the label carries no min-height and the visible track is h-6 (24px tall), where the control it replaces sat in a min-h-11 (44px) label.
> 
> `components/expense-editor.tsx:131`
> 
> Evidence: PR branch components/expense-editor.tsx:131 renders <label class="relative inline-flex shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center"> around an sr-only checkbox and an h-6 w-11 track, so the hit area is 24px tall; the replaced markup used <label class="flex min-h-11 items-center gap-2">. ui.md Density requires touch targets of at least 44px.
> 
> Fix: Give the IncludeSwitch label a 44px hit area (e.g. min-h-11 min-w-11 justify-center, or padding around the track) while keeping the checkbox-underneath payload exactly as is.

### Refused payment submissions now invalidate the home and activity caches although nothing changed: revalidateBalances(outcome.groupId) runs for every outcome with groupId undefined on refusals, and the undefined branch still calls revalidatePath('/') and revalidatePath('/activity'). Before, refusals returned early without revalidating anything.

> Refused payment submissions now invalidate the home and activity caches although nothing changed: revalidateBalances(outcome.groupId) runs for every outcome with groupId undefined on refusals, and the undefined branch still calls revalidatePath('/') and revalidatePath('/activity'). Before, refusals returned early without revalidating anything.
> 
> `lib/settle/actions.ts:215`
> 
> Evidence: PR branch lib/settle/actions.ts:123-130 makes groupId optional and always revalidates '/' and '/activity'; calls at :215 and :279 run unconditionally after withDb. Old code called revalidateBalances(access.group.id) only on the two success paths. Full suite passes either way (466 tests), so this is cache churn, not wrong data.
> 
> Fix: Only revalidate when something changed, e.g. gate the call on outcome.groupId being set, restoring the previous refusal behavior exactly.

## Found by QA — pre-existing

PR #43 did not introduce these, which is why they did not block it.

### Any refused expense save silently resets all split include switches to included

**Severity** minor (as judged by QA — reassess before planning).

**Expected.**
> A refused expense save keeps every input exactly as the user set it, including which members are left out of the split, so correcting the flagged field and retrying submits the intended split.

**Actual.**
> After any refused save, every split member's include switch reads included again, including members the user had deliberately left out. The refusal text, description, amount and per-member split values all persist; only the included choices are discarded. Reproduced 3/3 across two accounts and two refusal triggers (empty-split refusal and non-numeric-amount refusal).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Sign up as A, create a group, invite and join as B.
2. Open /groups/:id/expenses/new, fill amount 500 and any description.
3. Turn B's Include switch off (B reads excluded, A stays included).
4. Fill amount with not-a-number (or otherwise trigger a refused save) and press Add expense.
5. Observe the refusal; observe B's switch is silently back to included.

**Suspected cause.**
> The editor's state writers (changeParticipant and the field setters in _pr/components/expense-editor.tsx) preserve values across the useActionState refusal resync, but nothing re-applies the included flags after the action state resets them; the controlled checked={participant.included} binding plus the identical action wiring exist unchanged on the base commit, so this reads as a pre-existing state-resync defect, not a regression from this PR's IncludeSwitch restyle. A direct behavioral check on the base commit was attempted but the base preview wedges under Playwright traffic (health timeouts, aborted requests), so the call rests on the identical code architecture, not on a green base run.

**Reproducible:** always

### Activity excerpt renders long expense names as an untruncated link, scrolling the page at 375px

**Severity** minor (as judged by QA — reassess before planning).

**Expected.**
> No horizontal scroll on a phone viewport (qa_script viewport sweep); long names shorten instead of widening the page.

**Actual.**
> The activity entry renders the description as a plain untruncated link (class 'text-accent underline underline-offset-4', measured 1088px wide at x=105 on a 375px viewport), so the group page scrolls horizontally whenever a long expense name exists. The expense row itself (ListRow) truncates correctly.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Sign up, create a group, add an expense with a 140-character description.
2. Open the group page at 375px width.
3. document.documentElement.scrollWidth (1193) exceeds clientWidth (375); the widest element is the activity entry link to the expense edit page.

**Suspected cause.**
> components/activity-feed.tsx renders the expense description as raw link text with no truncation. That file is byte-identical between main and _pr (verified with diff), and the activity excerpt is explicitly a sibling piece in the work order out_of_scope list — pre-existing, found in passing.

**Reproducible:** always

---

**Check each one still reproduces before planning it.** They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong. Split this if they turn out to be unrelated.

Depends on #36.
